precepts.text: When Israel is in the midst of sin, God uses this language in the female context: she hath wearied herself with lies, and her great scum went not forth out of her. Definition read in class: scum is a layer of foul or unwanted matter that forms on top of a liquid, and informally a despised, immoral, or worthless person. That is the word God chose for his own people when the wickedness would not come out. Self examine, so that word never describes you.
precepts.point: She openeth her mouth with wisdom, and in her tongue is the law of kindness. This is the kind of wife you want. There was no kindness or wisdom in that email. Brothers, be mindful who you marry.

note.label: Agree Together | Bound Not Bondage

precepts.why:
“She openeth her mouth with wisdom; and in her tongue is the law of kindness.” That is the kind of wife you want, brothers. There was no kindness or wisdom in the email that attacked leadership over the one instance of a leader put out for adultery, while ignoring the three bishops and the seven or eight deacons who were in the midst of no such thing. For every solution we try to give, that spirit has two problems. That is not wife material; they are idolatrous women, some of them idolatrous evil black women, and they will try to destroy your life. Be mindful who you marry.

Now see what language God uses when Israel is in the midst of sin; he uses it in the female context: “She hath wearied herself with lies, and her great scum went not forth out of her”. There is one word that is often wanted but is hurtful to say, so God says it. Your scum is still in your mouth, sisters.

Scum is a layer of foul or unwanted matter that forms on top of a liquid, such as pond scum or soap scum. Informally it means a despised, immoral or worthless person or group, the scum of the earth. The slang meaning goes further: the epitome of a worthless, good-for-nothing human, at the bottom of the hierarchy of humans, possibly the worst word you can have your name associated with. It describes someone so disgraceful they are seen as the lowest form of life: worthlessness, a waste of skin, dirt, nothing. Because it is perfectly acceptable English and not a swear, it is even more demeaning; it is used only when it is the only word for the job, and it makes the victim feel like the lowest of the low.

That is the word God chose for his own people when she wore herself out with lies and the wickedness would not come out of her. Some of these evil sisters are the scum of the earth; that is what God is saying. So examine yourself, and open your mouth with wisdom and the law of kindness instead.

precepts.text: She openeth her mouth with wisdom, and in her tongue is the law of kindness. That is a sister who stays green. If that verse is not fulfilled in your house, that is why the house is not blessed. And 'can I explain myself' after admitting every charge is of the devil; correction cuts both ways, healing the one corrected and the one correcting.
precepts.point: He shall be as a tree planted by the waters, that spreadeth out her roots by the river, and shall not see when the heat cometh, but her leaf shall be green. Next to the water you never lack, and the sun does not burn you. Some brothers do not come to the war room for weeks because they do not want that water.

note.label: A Soul Without Purpose

precepts.why:
“Blessed is the man that trusteth in the Lord, and whose hope the Lord is. For he shall be as a tree planted by the waters, and that spreadeth out her roots by the river”. The one who trusts in the Lord and makes the Lord his hope, the Lord nourishes. A little plant next to a river never lacks water. When the heat comes the sun may be hot, but you will not feel it, because the hand of God covers you up. “but her leaf shall be green”: you stay green, you stay with wisdom.

Solomon shows what staying green looks like in a sister: “She openeth her mouth with wisdom; and in her tongue is the law of kindness.” That is a sister who stays in the green, the little plant by the water. When she opens her mouth, she opens it with wisdom, like someone who has understanding.

When that verse is not fulfilled in your house, that is why the house is not blessed. You wonder why you and your husband are going through things; that verse is not being fulfilled in that house.

The same goes for how we take correction. Asking to explain yourself after admitting to every charge is of the devil; Satan will make you look stupid, and it is better to just listen. The correction given is good for the one who gives it and the one who receives it. That knife cuts both ways: it cuts the one corrected, and the brother correcting says, I have to get my own thing together too. So do not be angry when a brother or sister checks you. Stay by the water and keep your leaf green.

precepts.text: Wine is for those of heavy hearts, to remember misery no more; that was Noah after the flood.
precepts.point: Ham saw the nakedness of his father and did not cover him; Shem and Japheth went backward and covered their father without looking. The commandments concerning nakedness were being applied; Leviticus 18 opens those laws.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

precepts.why:
“Give strong drink unto him that is ready to perish, and wine unto those that be of heavy hearts. Let him drink, and forget his poverty, and remember his misery no more.” Wine is for those of heavy hearts, and that was Noah after the flood.

He preached repentance for around a hundred years, and everyone he knew outside his house drowned. He drank too much, but he remained righteous in the eyes of the Most High.

precepts.text: Favour is deceitful and beauty is vain, but a woman that feareth the Lord, she shall be praised.
precepts.point: Favour is deceitful and beauty is vain. You are not going to look the same at seventy that you did at twenty-five; our days are threescore years and ten, or by reason of strength fourscore, and outside a handful who retain a semblance of their youth, the looks fade along the way. A woman that feareth the Lord, she shall be praised.

note.label: Genesis 29: Bone and Flesh in Haran

precepts.why:
Jacob “loved also Rachel more than Leah”, and he was showing more favor to Rachel because he was more attracted to Rachel. “And when the Lord saw that Leah was hated, he opened her womb: but Rachel was barren.”

“Favour is deceitful, and beauty is vain: but a woman that feareth the Lord, she shall be praised.” Favor built on looks is deceitful, and beauty is vain because it does not last: you are not going to look the same at seventy that you did at twenty-five. The looks fade along the way, and the woman worth praising is the one that feareth the Lord. Leah, the hated one, is the one whose womb the Lord opened.

precepts.text: Favour is deceitful and beauty is vain; Rachel's beauty did not keep her from being a thief.
precepts.point: Laban went to shear his sheep, and Rachel had stolen the images that were her father's. Remember what we read in Proverbs about beauty: yes, she was fine, but she was a thief. She might have been a fine thief, but she was a thief.

note.label: Genesis 31: The Return Home and Laban's Idols

precepts.why:
“Favour is deceitful, and beauty is vain: but a woman that feareth the Lord, she shall be praised.”

Remember that as Jacob rises up to return home to Isaac his father in the land of Canaan, and “Rachel had stolen the images that were her father’s.” Yes, she was fine, but she was a thief. She might have been a fine thief, but she was a thief. Her beauty did not keep her from stealing, and it is not beauty that earns praise but the fear of the Lord.

precepts.text: Who can find a virtuous woman? Her price is far above rubies and her husband safely trusts in her.
precepts.point: He that covers a transgression seeks love, but he that repeats a matter separates very friends. Covering sin like Ananias and Sapphira, who conspired to lie to the apostles, is condemned.

note.label: Proverbs 17: Trials That Refine and the Weight of Words

precepts.why:
“Who can find a virtuous woman? for her price is far above rubies.” The gift that is as a precious stone to him that has it is the virtuous woman: her price is far above rubies, and her husband safely trusts in her.

She is the silent and loving woman of Ecclesiasticus, a mind well instructed, priceless to the man who has her.

points: The words of king Lemuel, the prophecy that his mother taught him. This goes with Titus 2 and 3 about the aged women. Lemuel was a nickname for Solomon, so this is Bathsheba teaching Solomon.

note.label: When Children Walk in a Land of Shadows (Part 2)

points: What, my son? and what, the son of my womb? and what, the son of my vows? Give not thy strength unto women, nor thy ways to that which destroyeth kings. One of the first things she taught him was never give your strength to a woman. That is one thing young men must learn. Why does she teach it? Because she knows what is in women.

note.label: When Children Walk in a Land of Shadows (Part 2)

points: It is not for kings, O Lemuel, it is not for kings to drink wine; nor for princes strong drink: lest they drink, and forget the law, and pervert the judgment of any of the afflicted. So what kind of drinking is she talking about? Excess.

note.label: When Children Walk in a Land of Shadows (Part 2)

points: Give strong drink unto him that is ready to perish, and wine unto those that be of heavy hearts. When people are about to die, then you give them strong drink. And wine to those of heavy hearts — those filled with bitterness of soul, depressed.

note.label: When Children Walk in a Land of Shadows (Part 2)

points: Let him drink, and forget his poverty, and remember his misery no more. That is what happens in a lot of the black community and the Latin community as well. Alcohol is used as an escape.

note.label: When Children Walk in a Land of Shadows (Part 2)

points: Open thy mouth for the dumb in the cause of all such as are appointed to destruction. Open thy mouth, judge righteously, and plead the cause of the poor and needy.

note.label: When Children Walk in a Land of Shadows (Part 2)

points: She openeth her mouth with wisdom; and in her tongue is the law of kindness. There we go. Remember how I said his commandments — that is what comes out of you.

It did not say kindness. It said the law of kindness. That is your chaste conversation coupled with fear. This is your requirement as a wife to her husband. It is disciplined speech versus that uncontrolled, contentious tongue that you have.

note.label: SHE REVERENCE HER HUSBAND: Submission, Grace & Self-Examination of a Biblical Wife

points: Who can find a virtuous woman? for her price is far above rubies. There are a lot of sisters that are flippant about it — well, none of us is going to be that way. There are some that like to say they are in training, but they do not do any of the effort and the things I have spoken about today, because a lot of these scriptures you already know. I am not bringing out anything you have not heard before. Maybe, and this is my aim, I am trying to bring it out in a way where it is a little easier to apply and you have a better understanding of how it manifests itself physically.

While that price is far above rubies and very difficult to find, in the same chapter they tell you what you need to do to become that. It is like if you want to be a successful athlete and they say you have got to do this, you have got to be disciplined, you are going to arrive early and train this many times — and then if you have the discipline and conviction to do it, you become that. Obviously you have got to have the gifts as well. This virtuous woman is not unobtainable in these last days, because we have the manual right here. All you have got to do is drop your pride, stop being odious, and come back here and see how you model yourself. You can say, well, my mom was a whore and she did not teach me this and there are no good examples around me. You have it right here. So if you cannot see it in someone else, you see it here. It is not that complicated.

note.label: SHE REVERENCE HER HUSBAND: Submission, Grace & Self-Examination of a Biblical Wife

points: The heart of her husband doth safely trust in her, so that he shall have no need of spoil. She will do him good and not evil all the days of her life. And that does not just mean she is not going to cheat on him. It goes into everything we have spoken about up to this point. For me, if you are married, that should be a given, because it is one and done — you cheat on the man, you are out. So when it says doing good and not evil, everybody likes to stay on that, but it is going into the submission, the meek and quiet spirit, all of this.

note.label: SHE REVERENCE HER HUSBAND: Submission, Grace & Self-Examination of a Biblical Wife

points: She seeketh wool, and flax, and worketh willingly with her hands. So when she goes to do her woman's job — at this time it was wool and flax, it was a different time, things were obtained differently. Listen, it is the ideal situation that the wife does not work. But it is crazy out here. You cannot survive in a lot of cases without the two incomes, or the man has got to be doing exceptionally well. But that still does not change what the Lord requires of you.

note.label: SHE REVERENCE HER HUSBAND: Submission, Grace & Self-Examination of a Biblical Wife

points: She is like the merchants' ships; she bringeth her food from afar. So that means if she has got to commute an hour, she is going to commute an hour each way. Because these excuses that have come to us in councils — well, I am not like this because I have got to do this, this and this. No.

note.label: SHE REVERENCE HER HUSBAND: Submission, Grace & Self-Examination of a Biblical Wife

points: She riseth also while it is yet night, and giveth meat to her household, and a portion to her maidens. Meaning she held it down. She woke up early. She took care of her household and her maidens.

note.label: SHE REVERENCE HER HUSBAND: Submission, Grace & Self-Examination of a Biblical Wife

points: She considereth a field, and buyeth it: with the fruit of her hands she planteth a vineyard. Meaning she has sense. She was able to be out there and make important decisions, and her husband was able to trust in them.

note.label: SHE REVERENCE HER HUSBAND: Submission, Grace & Self-Examination of a Biblical Wife

points: She girdeth her loins with strength, and strengtheneth her arms. That does not mean she is out there trying to be manly. It means she has built herself up with the scriptures and she knows how to weather the emotional storm that she is inside, so that she can continue to do what she has got to do.

note.label: SHE REVERENCE HER HUSBAND: Submission, Grace & Self-Examination of a Biblical Wife

points: She perceiveth that her merchandise is good: her candle goeth not out by night. That goes into the same thing we read in Ephesians 4, that the sun does not set on your wrath. You do not lose your wisdom because you are out of the spirit. That is not an excuse.

note.label: SHE REVERENCE HER HUSBAND: Submission, Grace & Self-Examination of a Biblical Wife

points: She layeth her hands to the spindle, and her hands hold the distaff. So she can do fringes and work and buy food and cook the food. I should not bring my shirts and they sit there for two years before they are fringed. When I have some shirts she should not be like, oh my God, what are all these shirts. They get fringed.

note.label: SHE REVERENCE HER HUSBAND: Submission, Grace & Self-Examination of a Biblical Wife

points: She stretcheth out her hand to the poor; yea, she reacheth forth her hands to the needy. She is not afraid of the snow for her household: for all her household are clothed with scarlet. Meaning she made provision. She knows how to handle times — literally weathering the storm.

note.label: SHE REVERENCE HER HUSBAND: Submission, Grace & Self-Examination of a Biblical Wife

points: She maketh herself coverings of tapestry; her clothing is silk and purple. Her husband is known in the gates, when he sitteth among the elders of the land. Because he has a reputation based on his household as well as himself.

note.label: SHE REVERENCE HER HUSBAND: Submission, Grace & Self-Examination of a Biblical Wife

points: She maketh fine linen, and selleth it; and delivereth girdles unto the merchant. Strength and honour are her clothing. Where it says she girdeth her loins and strengtheneth her arms — here it says strength and honour are her clothing.

note.label: SHE REVERENCE HER HUSBAND: Submission, Grace & Self-Examination of a Biblical Wife

points: And she shall rejoice in time to come.

note.label: SHE REVERENCE HER HUSBAND: Submission, Grace & Self-Examination of a Biblical Wife

points: Because idolatry, hatred, malice, grudging, and bitterness corrupt a marriage one way or the other, a telegram was set up for sisters to send in letters with questions for the Marriage Is Honorable event tomorrow. One submission read in class asked how you can receive advice or approach leadership about your marriage issues when some of their marriages have the same issues or worse, pointing at the one instance of a leader put out for adultery. That email was not beneficial; it was an attack. There are three bishops and seven or eight deacons, and she ignores all the ones who were not in the midst of any such thing and highlights the one instance. For every solution we try to give, that spirit has two problems.
She openeth her mouth with wisdom, and in her tongue is the law of kindness. This is the kind of wife you want. There was no kindness or wisdom in that email. Brothers, be mindful who you marry.

note.label: Agree Together | Bound Not Bondage

points: Who can find a virtuous woman? for her price is far above rubies. The heart of her husband doth safely trust in her. This woman has shown this to her husband; he has observed her and he has no worries. Brothers, do you not want that? Sisters, do you not want to give that to your husband?

note.label: Agree Together | Bound Not Bondage

points: She will do him good and not evil all the days of her life. Teaching from the table: if a man at her job puts a hand on her, a virtuous wife handles that herself right there; she does not carry it home as a spark for her husband to catch a case over. Bishop's account: a brother called saying he was on his way to his wife's job to fight a man who grabbed her hand. The counsel: turn around, call your wife, and tell her she had better handle that; that is her job. Of course, if it is an assault she cannot stop, that is different; everybody understands that. But she will do him good and not evil means there are things she is supposed to shut down herself.

note.label: Agree Together | Bound Not Bondage

points: She riseth also while it is yet night, and giveth meat to her household: she is up early preparing for her household. She considereth a field, and buyeth it: she is investing for the household. She stretcheth out her hand to the poor. She is not afraid of the snow for her household: for all her household are clothed with scarlet. She is prepared.

note.label: Agree Together | Bound Not Bondage

points: She openeth her mouth with wisdom; and in her tongue is the law of kindness. She looketh well to the ways of her household, and eateth not the bread of idleness. Her household is her business and she is not idle.

note.label: Agree Together | Bound Not Bondage

points: Her children arise up, and call her blessed; her husband also, and he praiseth her. Who has to institute that in the house? The husband. You teach the children to honor their mother.

note.label: Agree Together | Bound Not Bondage

points: Who can find a virtuous woman? Cuz there's no more of them; it's these strong independent women now. For her price is far above rubies: if you find a woman that matches what virtue is, value her.

note.label: Are You A Strong Independent Woman?

points: The heart of her husband doth safely trust in her: you men that got women that want to keep these commandments, that's value God said is far above rubies, so don't mistreat them.

note.label: Are You A Strong Independent Woman?

points: She worketh willingly with her hands: because she's not there for a payday, to live off the man. She riseth also while it is yet night, and giveth meat to her household: she's concerned with being the way God designed her to be, a good wife to her husband and a caretaker of the home. This is what we need to instill in our women and bring that back.

note.label: Are You A Strong Independent Woman?

points: Favour is deceitful, and beauty is vain: but a woman that feareth the Lord, she shall be praised. In the world you may get favor because of your beauty, but it's deceitful, and your beauty is vanity cuz eventually you're going to get old. A woman that feareth the Lord shall be praised till the day that she dies.
A lot of these strong independent women on social media, everything is about their body and all they want is attention. But the woman of God is praised because of her attributes of God.

note.label: Are You A Strong Independent Woman?

points: Favour is deceitful and beauty is vain, but a woman that fears the Lord shall be praised.
A plate of food and a pretty face will deceive a man who does not look for her spirit.

note.label: Transforming from Immorality into Beautiful Civility Part 2

points: These are the words of King Lemuel, the prophecy his mother taught him. She warns her son not to give his strength to women nor his ways to that which destroys kings.

note.label: Proverbs 31: The Mother's Charge and the Virtuous Woman

note.label: Proverbs 31: The Mother's Charge and the Virtuous Woman

note.label: Proverbs 31: The Mother's Charge and the Virtuous Woman

points: She does not fear the snow, for her household is clothed in scarlet. Her clothing is silk and purple, her husband is known in the gates, and she sells the fine linen and girdles she makes.

note.label: Proverbs 31: The Mother's Charge and the Virtuous Woman

points: Strength and honor are her clothing and she rejoices in time to come. She opens her mouth with wisdom, her tongue carries the law of kindness, and she does not eat the bread of idleness.

note.label: Proverbs 31: The Mother's Charge and the Virtuous Woman

points: Her children rise up and call her blessed, and her husband praises her above all. Favor is deceitful and beauty is vain, but a woman who fears the Most High shall be praised and given the fruit of her own hands.
